# CLIFF — Benefits Cliff Navigator for Georgia Disability Families

> CLIFF is a free AI-powered platform helping Georgia families of children with disabilities prepare for the "benefits cliff" — critical transition points at ages 18 and 21 when eligibility rules, programs, and services change dramatically.

## What CLIFF Does

CLIFF provides free, personalized guidance on disability benefits, Medicaid waivers, and transition planning for Georgia families. The platform uses AI agents to help families understand their options and take action before critical deadlines.

## Who CLIFF Serves

- Georgia families with children or young adults with disabilities
- Parents preparing for the age 18 SSI transition
- Families navigating Katie Beckett / Deeming Waiver applications
- Caregivers seeking NOW, COMP, or SOURCE waiver information
- Families needing help with Medicaid, guardianship, and financial planning

## AI Agents

CLIFF uses 7 specialized AI agents:

1. **Intake Agent** — Conducts conversational intake interviews to understand each family's unique situation
2. **Research Agent** — Retrieves current Georgia disability benefits information and eligibility rules
3. **Advocacy Agent** — Tracks Georgia disability legislation and helps families contact representatives
4. **Proactive Agent** — Identifies upcoming deadlines and sends reminders for benefit transitions
5. **Document Intelligence Agent** — Helps families understand and prepare required documents
6. **Content Integrity Agent** — Verifies information accuracy against official Georgia sources
7. **Navigator Agent** — General-purpose assistant that coordinates across all other agents

## Key Topics Covered

### Medicaid Architecture (the hidden layers)
- Medicaid coverage vs. waiver funding — two separate streams with separate applications
- Medicaid as secondary payer — stacks with private/employer insurance to cover copays and gaps
- Section 1915(c) vs 1915(i) — slot-capped waivers vs uncapped state plan services
- Consumer direction / self-direction — families control the budget, hire their own workers
- Medicare vs Medicaid — dual eligibility pathway through SSDI after 24 months

### Georgia Waiver Programs
- NOW & COMP Waivers — DBHDD planning list, services, wait times for I/DD
- EDWP / CCSP — Elderly and Disabled Waiver for seniors 65+ and physically disabled
- SOURCE Waiver — integrated medical care and HCBS for SSI Medicaid recipients
- ICWP — Independent Care Waiver for adults 21+ with physical disabilities (TBI, spinal cord injury)
- Money Follows the Person (MFP) — transitioning from nursing homes/institutions to community living
- Structured Family Caregiving — paid family caregiver options under EDWP

### Benefits & Eligibility
- Supplemental Security Income (SSI) — eligibility, age 18 redetermination, application process
- Georgia Medicaid — pathways, coverage, transition from children's to adult programs
- Katie Beckett / Deeming Waiver — Level of Care statements, application guidance
- ABLE/STABLE Accounts — tax-advantaged savings up to $100K+ without affecting SSI/Medicaid
- Special Needs Trusts — unlimited asset protection
- PASS (Plan to Achieve Self-Support) — set aside income for work goals while keeping SSI

### Employment & Work Incentives
- Ticket to Work, Trial Work Period, Impairment Related Work Expenses
- Medicaid Buy-In for Workers with Disabilities — keep Medicaid while earning
- PASS — fund education, training, or business while maintaining benefits

### Additional Federal Programs
- Title XX Social Services Block Grant — respite, day services, home support through DFCS
- DD Act organizations — Georgia Advocacy Office, GCDD, UGA Institute on Human Development
- TRICARE ECHO — supplemental coverage for military family dependents with disabilities

### Crisis Services & Psychiatric Care
- DBHDD Crisis Services — 24/7 I/DD crisis homes, mobile crisis teams, GCAL (1-800-715-4225)
- CORE Behavioral Health — services for uninsured/underinsured Georgians
- PRTF (Psychiatric Residential Treatment) — Medicaid-covered youth psychiatric care, transition planning, MFP eligibility after 90 days

### Federal Benefit Overlays
- Disabled Adult Child (DAC) Benefits — Social Security on parent's record for adults disabled before 22
- DAC→Medicare pathway — dual eligibility after 24 months of DAC benefits
- EPSDT enforcement — federal mandate for medically necessary services for children under 21
- TRICARE Autism Care Demonstration — ABA therapy coverage for military dependents

### Housing
- Section 811 Supportive Housing — affordable integrated housing for adults with disabilities through DCA
- Housing Choice Vouchers (Section 8) — rent subsidies, long waitlists, apply to multiple authorities
- Mainstream Vouchers — set aside for non-elderly disabled adults

### Guardianship & Legal Decision-Making
- Full guardianship — Probate Court process, removes legal rights, last resort
- Supported decision-making — preserves autonomy, Georgia-recognized agreements
- Power of Attorney, advance directives, representative payee, conservatorship

### Appeals & Due Process
- Medicaid fair hearing process — 30-day window, continuation of benefits during appeal
- CMO grievance process — managed care appeal escalation
- EPSDT appeal leverage — federal mandate overrides state plan for children under 21

### Estate Recovery & Asset Protection
- Medicaid estate recovery — Georgia recovers long-term care costs after age 55
- Asset protection strategies — SNTs, ABLE accounts, home ownership planning
- Elder law attorney consultation guidance

### Education Transition & Pre-Employment
- IEP vs 504 Plan differences at age 18
- Pre-Employment Transition Services (Pre-ETS) under WIOA — available ages 14–22 even without IEP
- Georgia Vocational Rehabilitation coordination

### Waitlist Mechanics
- NOW/COMP Planning List vs Urgent List — prioritized system, not a queue
- Priority categories and estimated timelines
- How to update urgency status with DBHDD

### Legal Framework
- HCBS Settings Rule — federal compliance requirements for community-based settings
- Olmstead v. L.C. — community integration rights under ADA, legal leverage against institutionalization

### Transitions
- Age 18 Transition — SSI redetermination, guardianship alternatives, legal adulthood
- Age 21 Transition — EPSDT ending, IDEA aging out, adult service planning
- Two-track model: I/DD pathway (DBHDD) vs physical disability pathway (DCH)
- Cerebral palsy dual-track and autism-without-ID eligibility nuances

### Advocacy
- Georgia Disability Legislation — bill tracking, advocacy tools
- Long-Term Care Ombudsman — nursing home rights and complaints
- Georgia Advocacy Office — free legal help for Medicaid appeals
